sections.html:
Fountain is a home rule city in El Paso County, about 10 miles south of downtown Colorado Springs and just east of Fort Carson. Many sellers here have some link to the post. The city counted 29,802 residents in 2020 and 9,931 households, and the 2024 estimate of 29,457 shows a population that has barely moved. Of 10,324 housing units, only 3.8 percent stood empty, so a vacant house tends to stand out to neighbors and buyers alike.

Because the buyer pool stays about the same size, a house here competes on condition. Tidy, repaired homes win comparisons, and tired ones sit. A direct sale is one way around that contest.

sections.h2: El Paso County property tax payments
sections.html:
Payment optionDue date
Full paymentApril 30
First halfEnd of February
Second halfJune 15

Colorado's usual pattern is one payment by April 30, or two halves. To pay, use the treasurer's online portal, mail a check to P.O. Box 2018, Colorado Springs, CO 80901-2018, or visit the Citizens Service Center at 1675 West Garden of the Gods Road, Suite 2100. Counter hours run Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Owners who prefer smaller bites can enroll in monthly prepayment installments through EquaPay.

When a house is sold, the treasurer issues a Certificate of Taxes Due that shows where the parcel stands. Your title company normally orders it. For a payoff number of your own, call the treasurer at (719) 520-7900.

Prior-year balances deserve a hard look. Taxes left unpaid from an earlier year can be sold at the county's tax lien sale, and a lien on the parcel complicates any closing. Clear it, or let the title company pay it from your proceeds, before the deal gets near its final week. If a mortgage payoff also needs to come out of the proceeds, request that figure at the same moment, so the closing statement can show every deduction in one pass and you know your net amount well ahead of the signing appointment.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
Most of Fountain belongs to Fountain School District 8. The north end of the city is in Widefield School District 3, and thin slices of the north and south fall into Hanover District 28 and Harrison District 2.

  • Fountain District 8 covers most addresses.
  • Widefield District 3 covers the north end.
  • Hanover District 28 and Harrison District 2 touch small portions.

Buyers with children ask this early. Look up your parcel in the county data or ask the district, and give the right answer up front.

The city operates its own utility. City of Fountain Utilities dates to 1919 and supplies water and electric service to about 48,000 people in and around Fountain. The office is at 101 N Main St, and the phone is (719) 322-2010.

At a sale, you schedule a final meter reading and the buyer opens a new account. Call early, and do it sooner still if a past-due balance is on the account. The utility's customer tools include an outage map, bill assistance and utility easement information, plus a reminder to call 811 before digging. An easement across your yard can limit fences and additions, so tell the buyer about it.

Some buyers ask about PFAS contamination tied to a nearby Air Force base. The city said in 2020 that its water was safe to drink. Keep the city's water quality information close in case the question comes up.

Minor items hold up more closings than major ones. Tackle this list early.

  • Get your property tax status from the El Paso County Treasurer, and ask for a payoff figure if anything is unpaid.
  • Call City of Fountain Utilities at (719) 322-2010 to book the final reading.
  • Confirm the school district for your address.
  • Collect prior-owner paperwork, permits and repair receipts.
  • Settle who pays the Colorado deed fee and write it into the contract.

The state's documentary fee is one cent per $100 of consideration on a deed to real property, with any part of a hundred counted as a full one. The county clerk and recorder collects it, and a deal of $500 or less owes none. The purchase contract names who pays.

sections.h2: What a cash sale looks like in Fountain
sections.html:
Start by telling us about the house. After a review, you get an offer to take or leave. A title company then verifies ownership, orders the tax certificate and prepares the deed. With no lender in the picture, the closing date depends on the title work and on what you want.

Military families holding orders, heirs with an inherited house and landlords with an empty unit are among the people who ask about this route. We do not promise a price before seeing the property.

At the closing, you sign the deed, the county clerk and recorder records it, and the title company pays out your proceeds after taxes and any loan balance are settled. Buyers who pay cash take the house as it is, so repair bids and a lender's inspection list do not delay you.

sections.h2: Why sellers near Fort Carson pick a quick sale
sections.html:
Moves around a military installation are often set by orders, not by the housing market. A house that has to be sold before a report date cannot wait through weeks of showings and a buyer's loan approval. A direct sale lets you pick a closing date that matches the orders, and you can stay out of repair work in the final weeks before you leave.

Heirs and landlords face a similar clock. An inherited house costs money each month, and an empty rental brings in nothing. Weigh the offer against those carrying costs when you decide. Ask yourself what each extra month of ownership will really cost, then compare that total with the gap between a cash offer and a listing price.

sections.h2: From first call to closing day
sections.html:
Expect four stages. First comes a conversation about the property: its age, its condition, any liens and the timing you need. Second, the buyer looks the house over, in person or from photos. Third, you receive a written offer, and nothing obliges you to accept it. Fourth, the title company takes over paperwork, ordering the tax certificate and confirming that the deed can pass cleanly.

Bring identification, the loan servicer's contact details if a mortgage remains, and any HOA or utility account information you have. The more complete your folder is on day one, the fewer questions come up near the finish.

faqs.q: Is Fountain in El Paso County?
faqs.a: Yes. Fountain is a home rule city in El Paso County, about 10 miles south of downtown Colorado Springs. The county treasurer bills property taxes, and deeds are recorded with the county clerk and recorder.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Fountain house in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Fountain School District 8, the north is in Widefield District 3, and small parts fall into Hanover District 28 and Harrison District 2. Confirm your address with the district.

faqs.q: Who provides electricity and water in Fountain?
faqs.a: City of Fountain Utilities supplies both and serves about 48,000 people in and around the city. Call (719) 322-2010 to schedule a final reading when you sell.

faqs.q: How do I find out my property tax balance before closing?
faqs.a: Ask the El Paso County Treasurer for a payoff figure at (719) 520-7900, and have your title company order a Certificate of Taxes Due. Old unpaid balances can end up in the tax lien sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Fountain house if it needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not have to finish repairs first. The offer reflects the condition of the house.
